title: Present perfect 1 + countable and uncountable + which tense?
title_it: Present perfect 1 + countable e uncountable + quale tempo?
goal: Use the present perfect for news and results, choose between past simple, past continuous and present perfect, and use a / an, some / any and much / many.
goal_it: Usare il present perfect per notizie e risultati, scegliere tra past simple, past continuous e present perfect, e usare a / an, some / any e much / many.

steps.title: Present perfect: a link with the present
steps.title_it: Present perfect: un collegamento con il presente
en: We use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) when a past action matters now. We give news or talk about a result: I've lost my keys means I don't have them now.
We do not say when it happened. If we say a finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2019), we use the past simple instead.

Regular verbs: past participle = verb + -ed (finished, worked). Irregular verbs must be learned: buy - bought, see - seen, go - gone, write - written, eat - eaten, lose - lost, make - made, take - taken.
Careful, Italian speakers: the present perfect is NOT the same as the passato prossimo. In Italian you say 'ieri ho visto Anna', but in English you must say 'I saw Anna yesterday'.
it: Usiamo il present perfect (have / has + participio passato) quando un'azione passata conta adesso: diamo una notizia o parliamo di un risultato. I've lost my keys significa che adesso non le ho.
Non diciamo quando è successo. Se indichiamo un momento finito (yesterday, last week, in 2019) si usa il past simple.

Verbi regolari: participio passato = verbo + -ed (finished, worked). I verbi irregolari vanno imparati: buy - bought, see - seen, go - gone, write - written, eat - eaten, lose - lost, make - made, take - taken.
Attenzione: il present perfect NON è il passato prossimo italiano. In italiano si dice 'ieri ho visto Anna', ma in inglese si deve dire 'I saw Anna yesterday'.

examples.en: I've lost my phone. Can you call it?
examples.it: Ho perso il telefono. Puoi chiamarlo?

examples.en: They have bought a new flat.

steps.title: Present perfect: negative, questions, been / gone, just / already / yet
steps.title_it: Present perfect: negativa, domanda, been / gone, just / already / yet
en: Negative: haven't / hasn't + past participle (We haven't seen it). Question: Have / Has + subject + past participle? (Has she called?). Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't.
Been or gone? She has gone to Rome = she is in Rome now (or on the way). She has been to Rome = she went and came back. We use been for a visit that is finished.

Just = a very short time ago (I've just arrived). Already = earlier than expected (I've already eaten). Yet = until now, only in questions and negatives, at the end of the sentence (Have you finished yet? I haven't finished yet).
In British English we prefer the present perfect with just, already and yet. Do not use them with yesterday or last week.
it: Negativa: haven't / hasn't + participio passato (We haven't seen it). Domanda: Have / Has + soggetto + participio passato? (Has she called?). Risposte brevi: Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't.
Been o gone? She has gone to Rome = è a Roma adesso (o sta andando). She has been to Rome = ci è andata ed è tornata. Usiamo been per una visita conclusa.
Just = poco fa (I've just arrived). Already = prima del previsto (I've already eaten). Yet = finora, solo in domande e negative, alla fine della frase (Have you finished yet? I haven't finished yet).
In inglese britannico con just, already e yet si preferisce il present perfect. Non si usano con yesterday o last week.

examples.en: Mark has gone to the bank. He'll be back soon.
examples.it: Mark è andato in banca. Torna presto.

examples.en: I've been to the bank. Now I'm at home.
examples.it: Sono stato in banca. Ora sono a casa.

examples.en: We haven't seen the new film yet.
examples.it: Non abbiamo ancora visto il film nuovo.

steps.title: Which tense? Past simple, past continuous or present perfect
steps.title_it: Quale tempo? Past simple, past continuous o present perfect
en: Ask yourself three questions. 1) Is there a finished time (yesterday, last night, in 2019, three days ago)? Use the past simple. 2) Was the action in progress at a moment in the past, or is it the background of a story, or was it interrupted (while, when)? Use the past continuous. 3) Is there no finished time and the action matters now (just, already, yet, ever, never, so far, this week)? Use the present perfect.
Clue words: yesterday and last night call for the past simple; while calls for the past continuous; just, already and yet call for the present perfect.
A finished time and the present perfect NEVER go together: I have seen him yesterday is wrong. Say I saw him yesterday.
it: Fatti tre domande. 1) C'è un momento finito (yesterday, last night, in 2019, three days ago)? Past simple. 2) L'azione era in corso a un momento del passato, è lo sfondo di una storia o è stata interrotta (while, when)? Past continuous. 3) Non c'è un momento finito e l'azione conta adesso (just, already, yet, ever, never, so far, this week)? Present perfect.
Parole spia: yesterday e last night chiamano il past simple; while chiama il past continuous; just, already e yet chiamano il present perfect.
Un momento finito e il present perfect NON vanno mai insieme: I have seen him yesterday è sbagliato. Si dice I saw him yesterday.

head: Tense
Use
Clue words
Example
rows: I was walking when I lost my keys.
link with now, no definite time
I've lost my keys. I can't get in.

examples.en: I was watching a film when you called.
examples.it: Stavo guardando un film quando hai chiamato.

steps.title: Countable and uncountable nouns: a / an, some / any, much / many
steps.title_it: Nomi countable e uncountable: a / an, some / any, much / many
en: Countable nouns can be counted: a banana, two bananas. Uncountable nouns cannot be counted and have no plural: rice, water, music, money, sugar, bread, milk.
Use a / an only with a singular countable noun (a banana, an orange). Plural countable nouns and uncountable nouns stand alone, or take some / any: I like bananas. I eat rice. We need some sugar.
some = a certain amount, in positive sentences and offers (Would you like some tea?). any = in negatives and questions (There isn't any milk. Is there any bread?).

many + countable plural (How many eggs?). much + uncountable (How much milk?). a lot of works with both. In positive sentences we usually say a lot of. For quantities use containers: a cup of tea, a bowl of rice, a loaf of bread.
it: I nomi countable si possono contare: a banana, two bananas. Gli uncountable non si contano e non hanno plurale: rice, water, music, money, sugar, bread, milk.
A / an solo con un countable singolare (a banana, an orange). I countable plurali e gli uncountable stanno da soli o con some / any: I like bananas. I eat rice. We need some sugar.
some = una certa quantità, nelle frasi positive e nelle offerte (Would you like some tea?). any = nelle negative e nelle domande (There isn't any milk. Is there any bread?).

many + countable plurale (How many eggs?). much + uncountable (How much milk?). A lot of va con entrambi. Nelle frasi positive di solito si dice a lot of. Per le quantità si usano i contenitori: a cup of tea, a bowl of rice, a loaf of bread.

examples.en: There aren't many chairs in the living room.
examples.it: Non ci sono molte sedie in soggiorno.

examples.en: Is there any bread in the kitchen?
How much money have you got?

steps.q: Oh no! I ___ my phone. I can't find it.
steps.q_it: Oh no! Ho perso il telefono. Non lo trovo.
steps.why: No finished time, and the result matters now (I don't have it): present perfect.
steps.why_it: Nessun momento finito e il risultato conta adesso (non ce l'ho): present perfect.

steps.q: Anna ___ (finish) her homework. Now she can watch TV.
steps.q_it: Anna ha finito i compiti. Ora può guardare la TV.
steps.why: Anna is she: has + finished. The result matters now.
steps.why_it: Anna è she: has + finished. Il risultato conta adesso.

steps.q: They ___ (buy) a new flat in the city centre.
steps.q_it: Hanno comprato un appartamento nuovo in centro.
steps.why: Buy is irregular: bought. They takes have.
steps.why_it: Buy è irregolare: bought. They vuole have.

steps.q: We ___ (not / see) the new film yet.
steps.q_it: Non abbiamo ancora visto il film nuovo.
steps.why: Negative: haven't + past participle. See is irregular: seen.
steps.why_it: Negativa: haven't + participio passato. See è irregolare: seen.

steps.q: Mark isn't in the office. He ___ to the bank. He'll be back soon.
steps.q_it: Mark non è in ufficio. È andato in banca. Torna presto.
steps.why: He is still at the bank, so we use gone. Been means he went and came back.
steps.why_it: È ancora in banca, quindi si usa gone. Been vuol dire che è andato ed è tornato.

steps.q: Hi! I'm back from the shops. I ___ to the shops and I bought some bread.
steps.q_it: Ciao! Sono tornato dai negozi. Sono stato ai negozi e ho comprato del pane.
steps.why: The speaker went and came back, so we use been.
steps.why_it: Chi parla è andato ed è tornato, quindi si usa been.

steps.q: Is Lisa here? No, she hasn't arrived ___.
steps.q_it: Lisa è qui? No, non è ancora arrivata.
steps.why: Yet goes at the end of a negative sentence: not until now.
steps.why_it: Yet va in fondo a una frase negativa: finora no.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: I have just seen your sister
steps.why: Subject + have + just + past participle.
steps.why_it: Soggetto + have + just + participio passato.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine (è una domanda).
steps.why: Question: Has + subject + past participle, and yet at the end.
steps.why_it: Domanda: Has + soggetto + participio passato, e yet in fondo.

steps.q: Which word is uncountable?
steps.q_it: Quale parola è uncountable?
steps.why: We cannot count rice and it has no plural. We say a bowl of rice.
steps.why_it: Rice non si conta e non ha plurale. Si dice a bowl of rice.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
options: I have a rice for lunch.
I have some rice for lunch.
I have an rice for lunch.
steps.why: Rice is uncountable: no a / an and no plural. We use some or nothing.
steps.why_it: Rice è uncountable: niente a / an e niente plurale. Si usa some o niente.

steps.q: She is eating ___ orange.
steps.q_it: Sta mangiando un'arancia.
steps.why: Orange is countable and singular, and it starts with a vowel sound: an.
steps.why_it: Orange è countable singolare e comincia con un suono vocale: an.

steps.q: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
steps.q_it: Non c'è latte in frigo.
steps.why: Negative sentence with an uncountable noun: any.
steps.why_it: Frase negativa con un uncountable: any.

steps.q: We need ___ sugar for the cake. Can you buy it?
steps.q_it: Ci serve dello zucchero per la torta. Puoi comprarlo?
steps.why: Positive sentence: some.
steps.why_it: Frase positiva: some.

steps.q: How ___ people live in your building?
steps.q_it: Quante persone abitano nel tuo palazzo?
steps.why: People is countable plural: how many.
steps.why_it: People è countable plurale: how many.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: There aren't many chairs in the room
steps.why: There aren't + many + countable plural.
steps.why_it: There aren't + many + countable plurale.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine (è un'offerta).
steps.why: In offers we use some, even in a question.
steps.why_it: Nelle offerte si usa some, anche in una domanda.

steps.q: I ___ to Paris last summer.
steps.q_it: Sono andato a Parigi l'estate scorsa.
steps.why: Last summer is a finished time: past simple. Not the present perfect.
steps.why_it: Last summer è un momento finito: past simple, non present perfect.

steps.q: Help! I ___ my wallet. Can you look for it with me?
steps.q_it: Aiuto! Ho perso il portafoglio. Mi aiuti a cercarlo?
steps.why: No finished time, and the problem is now: present perfect.
steps.why_it: Nessun momento finito e il problema è adesso: present perfect.

steps.q: We ___ (see) that film yesterday. It was great.
steps.q_it: Abbiamo visto quel film ieri. Era bellissimo.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time: past simple, saw.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un momento finito: past simple, saw.

steps.q: While we ___ lunch, the phone rang.
steps.q_it: Mentre pranzavamo, il telefono ha squillato.
steps.why: While + an action in progress: past continuous. The phone ringing is the short action.
steps.why_it: While + azione in corso: past continuous. Il telefono che squilla è l'azione breve.

steps.q: A: Is Ben at home? B: No, he ___ (just / leave).
steps.q_it: A: Ben è a casa? B: No, è appena uscito.
steps.why: Just plus a link with now: has just left.
steps.why_it: Just più un legame con adesso: has just left.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
steps.why: Yesterday needs the past simple. Present perfect with yesterday is a very common mistake.
steps.why_it: Yesterday vuole il past simple. Present perfect con yesterday è un errore molto comune.

steps.q: Where ___ you go last weekend?
steps.q_it: Dove sei andato lo scorso weekend?
steps.why: Last weekend: past simple. Question: did + subject + infinitive.
steps.why_it: Last weekend: past simple. Domanda: did + soggetto + infinito.

steps.q: When I arrived, they ___ dinner in the kitchen.
steps.q_it: Quando sono arrivato, stavano preparando la cena in cucina.
steps.why: They were in the middle of the action when I arrived: past continuous.
steps.why_it: Erano nel mezzo dell'azione quando sono arrivato: past continuous.

steps.q: How ___ do you go to the gym? Twice a week.
steps.q_it: Quanto spesso vai in palestra? Due volte a settimana.
steps.why: Twice a week is about frequency: how often.
steps.why_it: Twice a week parla di frequenza: how often.

cards.ex: He has gone to the bank. I've been to the bank.
rice is uncountable, banana is countable
There isn't any milk. We need some sugar.
How many eggs? How much milk? A lot of people.
a cup of tea, a loaf of bread
